group.passage:
Founded in southeastern India in 1968, Auroville is a rural community that promises a utopian dream of human unity and equality. [[1]] The community itself has won the support of the Indian government and the recognition of UNESCO. It’s viewed as an experiment of humanity aiming to satisfy the needs of mankind. The population of Auroville has been on a steady increase since its establishment, with about one third of the residents being local Indians. [[2]]
However, in recent years, a vocal group of inhabitants headed by Jayanti Ravi, a civil servant, spoke about their frustration with the lack of progress and improvement within the community, crying for an update on the masterplan of development conceived decades earlier. [[3]] Opposition to Ravi came primarily from younger Aurovillians who took it upon themselves to stick to the original ideal of Auroville.
For the time being, Ravi and her followers seem to have an upper hand, with the government on their side. [[4]] Violent clashes have become increasingly common, and more and more are convinced that achieving real unity or at least finding common ground is highly unlikely in the near future. Only time will tell.

options_bank.A: They lead a self-sufficient life, living on organic farms, dairies, and orchards on community areas designated as “Green Belt.”
options_bank.B: Being quite familiar with how politics works also gives her a great edge over the younger and thus less seasoned or experienced Aurovillians.
options_bank.C: They argued for the need to upsize the community to welcome and embrace new residents and pushed for modern practices of agriculture.
options_bank.D: It aspires to be a town where residents live in peace and harmony, in the spirit of cooperation, regardless of their gender, religion and nationality.

tags.topic: Auroville, a utopian community in India, and the conflict over its development
